question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹500. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 24% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) is directly calculated as 124% of the Cost Price (CP) since the profit is 24%.

SP = 124% of 500

SP = 1.24 × 500 = 620

**∴ The correct answer is ₹620.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹500

Profit = 24%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP = ₹500
 100%
 
 SP = ₹620
 124%
 
• 
 +24% Profit
 (+ ₹120)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 500 × (100 + 24) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 500 × (124 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 5 × 124

⇒ SP = 620

**∴ The correct answer is ₹620.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When an article is sold at a loss, the Selling Price = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Successive Profit

The net change for two successive profits of a% and b% is given by the formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.
